description:
EPIC. Maintainer ask 2026-09-04: for each well-documented test reactor we validate against, a small agent (Haiku, or ChatGPT with a Python interpreter and shell) should be able to drive the whole chain through the outram-park-backend Python API, within reasonable compute.

THE PIPELINE, and where each stage stands. Surveyed 2026-09-04, not assumed.

  1. ENDF -> pointwise data. njoy-outram-park-fork. Tape::read_file, reconr, doppler_broaden all reach Python as of 5cab9ef. EndfCache can fetch. STATUS: seams exist; DATA does not (see below).
  2. Monte Carlo. outram-mc-libs. run_keff_csg on arbitrary CSG, run_keff_mg, run_fixed_source, TRISO into_geometry, CRP pebble packing, delta tracking. STATUS: works — a Godiva-like sphere assembled from Python gives k = 1.00485 +/- 0.00541.
  3a. MGXS. STATUS: DOES NOT EXIST. Mgxs::new has no call site outside its own definition; there are no MGXS tallies; Mgxs and genfoam GroupConstants are different types with no converter. Split out as op-84bc / gh:#42.
  3b. Feedback coefficients. teh-o-prke has Nordheim-Fuchs, Doppler, control-rod and moderator-density feedback. STATUS: NordheimFuchs is NOT exposed to Python (confirmed missing from the wheel). Doppler/rod feedback partially.
  4. Deterministic. genfoam neutronics (diffusion/SP3/SN/point-kinetics on FvMesh), bedok nodal, moltres for circulating fuel. STATUS: present in Rust; Python coverage thin (moltres 14 classes / 1 function, onix 10 / 1).
  5. ROM / surrogate. raffles. STATUS: **surrogate.rs is 54 lines with NO pub items — a stub.** sensitivity.rs has Sobol layout, Pearson/Spearman correlation and Sobol sampling, but there is no surrogate model of any kind: no GP, no polynomial chaos, no POD. THIS STAGE DOES NOT EXIST AND BLOCKS EVERY REACTOR.
  6. Digital twin. outram-park-digital-twin-engine. STATUS: exists, but plant models live in example trees (11,531 lines for htgr_sim_v1) and are reachable from nothing — see the placement note on op-jyyp.

TWO FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE WHOLE EPIC.

FINDING A — stage 5 is a stub. The pipeline as described has a hole in the middle-late position. Either implement a surrogate in raffles (the sampling and sensitivity halves are already there, so this is the model itself: GP or polynomial chaos over the state grid), or drop stage 5 from the near-term chain and go straight from deterministic to twin. That is a maintainer decision and should be made before any reactor child starts, because it changes every one of them.

FINDING B — we do not have the nuclear data. reference-data/endf holds 12 files: U-235, U-238, H-2, He-4, Ar-37, and TSLs for Al-27, C-in-SiC, Si-in-SiC, crystalline graphite, reactor graphite 10P/30P, H-in-ZrH. MISSING for the named reactors: O-16 (every oxide fuel), H-1 (all light water), Zr, Fe/Cr/Ni, B-10, Pu-239/240/241, Na-23, Li-7/Be-9/F-19 (MSRE salt), Th-232/U-233. Stage 1 is therefore a real per-reactor task, not a formality; EndfCache is the seam to drive it.

COMPUTE BUDGET IS PART OF THE SPEC. 'Reasonable compute' has to be written down per reactor or a small agent will launch something that never finishes. Each child must state a target: particles x generations for the MC stage, group structure and state-grid size for MGXS, and a wall-clock ceiling. A pebble bed with double heterogeneity is orders of magnitude past a bare sphere and cannot be scoped by analogy to one.

REACTORS, and the existing work each must NOT duplicate:
  HTR-10   -> op-jyyp (18 children, 0 done), docs/reactor-scoping/htr10*.md
  HTTR     -> op-id3l.4 (first criticality + rod worth), .9 (core TH), .11 (LOFC)
  MSRE     -> op-6w0 (digital twin epic), docs/reactor-scoping/msre.md
  EBR-II   -> docs/reactor-scoping/ebr2.md
  EBR-I    -> nothing yet
  LWR      -> op-wqk.10 (ipwr_sim_v1), op-wqk.11 (abwr_sim_v1), docs ipwr.md / bwr.md
  HWR      -> nothing yet

Children are the per-reactor validation runs. They are validation and API-exercise tasks, NOT simulator-construction tasks — the simulators are the epics above and this epic depends on them rather than replacing them.

NO V&V IS CLAIMED BY THIS EPIC. Producing a number for a benchmark is not validating against it; each child names its published reference and its acceptance band explicitly, and a child that runs but misses its band is a finding, not a pass.

Related: op-375p / gh:#41 (neutronics API scope), op-84bc / gh:#42 (MGXS), op-m2mj (Haiku harness).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
gh:#43 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/43

Children: op-q2ec (stage 5 decision), op-mug0 (stage 1 ENDF), op-9lp1 HTR-10, op-p5j1 HTTR, op-lp3b MSRE, op-owb7 EBR-I, op-jhjy EBR-II, op-3xen LWR, op-x7uc HWR.

PRE-EXISTING SIBLING FOUND: op-cpz 'Validate self-shielded MGXS + URR PENDF reader vs a real NJOY GENDF golden tape'. That is the nuclear-data-side validation of the same MGXS chain as op-84bc / gh:#42. Do not duplicate it — a GENDF golden-tape comparison is a stronger check on the collapse than our own three-route k-eff consistency test, because it is against an external reference rather than against ourselves. Sequence op-cpz before or alongside op-84bc.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Stage 5 (op-q2ec) is now scoped in its own bead op-38my / gh:#44 — 'Reduced-order models / surrogates: absent in raffles, needed in tampines'.

Two things that only became clear on survey and that change how the gate should be read:
  * raffles is a RAVEN port and ROM is RAVEN's OWN first-class concept, so the stub is a gap in the port, not merely a missing pipeline stage.
  * raffles has a named owner (Adolphus Lye) and the crate docs say direction is their call. The stage-5 decision is therefore partly a governance routing, not purely technical.
  * tampines needs a tabulation layer for real-time twin operation regardless of what the pipeline decides.

op-q2ec remains this epic's gate; the work and the decision live in op-38my.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Seven V&V information-request issues filed and labelled V&V: gh:#47 HTR-10 (op-9lp1), #48 HTTR (op-p5j1), #49 MSRE (op-lp3b), #50 EBR-II (op-jhjy), #51 EBR-I (op-owb7, tagged human-audit — repo argues against it, recommend closing), #52 LWR (op-3xen), #53 HWR (op-x7uc).

Each lists ONLY what cannot be obtained from the repository, and each points at the existing 'Open questions for the maintainer' sections in docs/reactor-scoping/ rather than re-asking them.

TWO GATING ANSWERS decide whether their reactors are validation cases at all:
  * MSRE — msre.md section 7 asks whether moltres needs human V&V sign-off before anything depends on it. It is currently untrusted draft material. If it cannot be depended on there is no MSRE validation run.
  * EBR-II — ebr2.md section 7 asks whether the IAEA CRP benchmark specification is actually obtainable. That is a yes/no that decides validation vs demonstration.

RECOMMENDED FIRST RUN remains the LWR pin cell (gh:#52), ahead of any headline reactor: cheapest end-to-end exercise of all six stages, and every stage should work, so a failure is a pipeline defect rather than a physics gap.

title: Validation pipeline per test reactor: ENDF -> MC -> MGXS+feedback -> deterministic -> ROM -> digital twin
